reasoning_text:
We need to design LSTM weights that forecast next-day sales. Key structure: sales series with trend upward (from ~100 to ~120 over 560 days) plus noise, promotions add boost? Actually promotion flag: on promotion days sales are often higher... looking at data: day 8 flag=1 sales 115.82 (high), day 24 flag 1 sales 113.91 high, day 30 flag1 127.76 high, day 46 flag1 124.41, day 70 flag1 108.87... Hmm some promo days high. But note flag for the day being forecast is in the last input row. So the model can use promo flag of day t to adjust prediction.

Simpler approach: make LSTM compute a weighted average of recent normalized values, plus promo adjustment. Since we can't run code, we need a design whose behavior we can reason about analytically.

Easiest robust design: make the LSTM essentially an exponential moving average of the normalized value, with output = EMA (predict mean), plus promo boost added via the flag input on the last step.

Design: make gates so that c accumulates a running average. Alternative: make h track x (the value) via linear behavior, and have a separate unit track promo.

Let me think: we want prediction â level (recent average, maybe last ~10-20 days) + promo_effect if flag=1.

Actually what's the promo effect? Compare promo days vs non-promo. Let's check some: promo days sales: 115.82, 113.91, 127.76, 124.41, 108.87(?), 112.36, 117.11, 117.84, 114.16, 118.19, 110.42(1), 115.62, 121.01, 115.41, 123.78, 114.80, 120.53, 118.76, 116.20, 117.50, 131.71, 114.71, 128.84, 114.58, 117.00, 128.83, 124.97, 120.39, 110.75, 133.85, 122.73, 115.18, 127.61, 127.70, 120.61, 117.04, 119.55, 122.23, 139.61, 136.13, 130.91, 133.03, 124.71, 140.94, 124.91, 135.53, 115.21, 126.65, 121.46, 122.59, 120.39, 124.03, 117.46, 119.01, 124.26, 123.23, 130.30, 124.21, 125.96, 133.54, 119.10, 116.98, 141.55, 127.82, 131.10, 128.00, 121.86, 133.67, 134.23, 133.72, 128.42, 129.51, 129.99...

Non-promo days nearby are ~105-120. Promo effect seems roughly +10? E.g., day 139.61 at 327 vs neighbors ~100. That's huge. Promo effect maybe +15? Actually noise is large too (non-promo days range 92-130). Let's estimate: promo days mean maybe ~124 overall; non-promo mean maybe ~110. But there's trend, and promos more frequent later. Promo boost maybe ~+10-15. Let's assume +12.

But careful: maybe promo causes a dip after? Day 327 promo 139.61, day 328 99.93. Day 362 promo 140.94, day 363 100.36. Day 488 promo 141.55, day 489 106.20. Hmm interestingâday before promo also high sometimes? Day 326 115.12, day 361 123.37. The promo day value high and next day low-ish. But we only need the promo day value.

Also note the value in row k is sales of day s and promo flag of day s+1. The last row has value of day t-1 and promo flag of day t (the day being predicted). So when predicting day t, we know if day t is promo.

Wait â interesting: maybe the promo flag of day t-1... the value on day t-1 already reflects promo of t-1. Fine.

So target: predict y_t = level_t + promo_t * boost + noise. Also there might be a "post-promo dip": day after promo tends low. E.g., day 552 promo 129.51, day 553 104.12 â dip. Day 448 promo 124.21, day 449 109.17. Day 519 promo 128.00, day 520 promo 121.86, day 521 106.83. So after promo there's a dip of maybe -8. This matters: when day t-1 was promo, the value y_{t-1} is high; our EMA will be biased up. Also y_t itself may dip. We could handle: subtract when previous day promo... but the input row structure: row k has value day s and flag day s+1. So flag of day s+1 paired with value of day s. The last row: value t-1, flag t. Second-to-last: value t-2, flag t-1. So we know flag_{t-1} paired with value t-2 â that tells us whether the last known value y_{t-1} was a promo day (flag_{t-1} appears in the second-to-last row). Hmm, actually flag of day t-1 is in row for s = t-2. Yes.

This is getting complex. Simpler: build model that predicts level via EMA of values, plus boost for flag_t. Optionally correct promo-day values before averaging: subtract boost from values on promo days. But value s and flag s are not in same row! Row k: [value_s, flag_{s+1}]. So value_s's promo status is flag_s, which is in row k-1. That's an off-by-one pairing â annoying but LSTM can handle: memory of flag from previous step.

Given complexity and no execution, maybe simplest good-enough: EMA prediction + promo boost on output for flag_t. The promo-day contamination of EMA is a minor issue (promos ~15% of days, each inflates EMA by boost*weight).

Let's design weights concretely.

Plan:
- Unit 0..: value pathway. Let input x = [v, p] where v normalized value, p promo flag.
- We want c0 (cell of unit 0) to be EMA of v with some rate, and h0 = tanh(c0)... but tanh nonlinearity. Keep c0 small so tanh(c0)âc0? tanh is decently linear near 0 but v ranges: normalized v = (y-100)/20, ranges from about -0.4 to 2. Trend: mean normalized goes from ~0 to ~0.6. Values up to ~2. tanh(2)=0.964, error. Hmm.

Alternative: use output gate to keep h = o*tanh(c). We can scale: put v scaled down by factor, e.g., accumulate c = 0.1*v + 0.9*c... then h via tanh(c) with c in [-0.2, 0.2] fine, then scale up in W_out. Or just accept tanh compression? Let's do scaling.

Actually simpler linear design: set forget gate â constant Î± (via bias, no weights), input gate â constant Î², cell gate g â v * s where s scales. With iÂ·g = Î²Â·sÂ·v. Set Î²Â·s = 1-Î±. Then c_t = Î± c + (1-Î±) v (if v is the scaled version? no, v raw normalized). Then h = oÂ·tanh(c). Set o â 1 (bias large). tanh(c): c ranges roughly [-0.4, 2]... Actually EMA of normalized value ~ mean around 0 to 0.8, with daily noise std maybe 0.35. EMA c roughly in [-0.2, 1.2] at the end. tanh compresses: tanh(1.2)=0.833 vs 1.2. That's bad.

Better: scale v by 0.5 in the cell path: c = Î± c + (1-Î±)(0.5 v). Then c in ~[0,0.6]. tanh(0.6)=0.537 vs 0.6 â 10% error, still compresses nonlinearly. Nonlinearity distorts level estimates as level rises â but we could just accept and calibrate? Risky.

Alternative: use output gate to counteract? h = oÂ·tanh(c); can't invert tanh with fixed o.

Alternative approach: use a "linear readout of last value plus correction". Actually maybe simpler: predict y_t â y_{t-1} + promo adjustments? But daily noise std is large (~5-8?), so prediction from last value alone has that noise. EMA over ~5-10 days reduces noise. The trend is slow.

Alternative: avoid tanh by making c very small and amplifying at output. c small: c = Î± c + (1-Î±)Â·kÂ·v with k=0.1. Then c â 0.1Â·EMA(v), in range ~[-0.05, 0.1]. tanh(c)âc (error <1%). Then W_out scale by 10. 

Let's set: unit 0: forget bias f0 such that sigmoid(f0)=Î±. Choose Î±: effective averaging window. Noise per day std: let's estimate. Non-promo values fluctuate Â±6 around trend. EMA with rate (1-Î±) over N=1/(1-Î±) days. If noise iid Ïâ6 (in original units), EMA noise = ÏÂ·sqrt((1-Î±)/(2-Î±)) â ÏÂ·sqrt((1-Î±)/(1+Î±))... For Î±=0.8: sqrt(0.2/1.8)=0.333 â 2.0. For Î±=0.9: sqrt(0.1/1.9)=0.23â1.4. But trend: level rises ~20 over 560 days â 0.036/day. EMA lags by Î±/(1-Î±) days â 9 days for Î±=0.9 â lag 0.32. Negligible-ish. Also promo contamination: promo boost ~+13 occurs ~13% of days; EMA bias = 0.13Â·13Â·(weights)... In steady state EMA includes promo days: E[v] = level + 0.13Â·boost. So EMA overestimates level by ~1.7. Hmm. We could subtract boost on promo days before averaging: we know flag_{s} in previous row. Doable: keep a memory of previous flag, and subtract from v when flag was 1.

Alternatively, just fit intercept: predict EMA + promo_tÂ·boost - 1.7. But when day t is promo we add boost; when not, subtract 1.7 bias... but bias exists regardless. Fine, constant offset.

Also promo days might be followed by dip (pull-forward). Check: day after promo vs level. Day 9: 95.97 vs ~103 level â dip ~-7. Day 25: 97.33 vs ~103 â -6. Day 31: 102.68 vs ~103 â 0. Day 47: 109.78 vs ~100 â +10? Hmm. Day 71: 90.52 vs ~100 â -10. Day 553: 104.12 vs ~115 â -11. Mixed. There seems to be a dip after promo of maybe -5. But also promos often come in pairs (day 91,92; 260,261; 321... 477,478; 519,520). 

Let's quantify promo boost more carefully. Compare promo day value to local average of surrounding non-promo days.

Early era: day 8: 115.82; neighbors ~100-108 â +12. Day 24: 113.91 vs ~100 â +14. Day 30: 127.76 vs ~100 â +25 (noise). Day 46: 124.41 vs ~98 â +26. Day 70: 108.87 vs ~98 â +11. Day 78: 117.11 vs ~102 â +15. Day 80: 117.84 â +15. Day 88: 114.16 vs ~92 â +22. Day 91: 118.19, 92: 110.42 vs ~95 â +23, +15. Day 101: 121.01 vs ~100 â +21. Day 194: 131.71 vs ~105 â +26. Day 327: 139.61 vs ~105 â +35?? Day 334: 136.13 vs ~108 â +28. Day 362: 140.94 vs ~107 â +34. Day 369: 135.53. Day 488: 141.55 vs ~112 â +29. Day 522: 133.67 vs ~112 â +22. Day 542: 133.72. Day 552: 129.51.

Hmm, promo boost seems to grow over time? Early +12-15, late +25-35? Or the trend is nonlinear. Actually the baseline also rises. Let's compare: around day 550, non-promo ~110-120 (e.g., 543:115.90, 544:129.62, 545:116.26, 547:110.37, 548:116.30, 549:117.62, 550:120.56, 551:128.61, 553:104.12, 554:111.99, 555:110.58, 556:112.75, 558:117.42, 559:109.62). Mean ~115. Day 552 promo: 129.51 â +15. Day 557 promo 129.99 â +15. Day 546 promo 128.42 â +13. Day 536 promo 134.23 â +19. Day 519 promo 128.00 vs ~113 â +15. Day 505: 127.82 vs ~110 â +18. Day 508: 131.10 â +21.

So promo boost ~+15 in original = 0.75 normalized units. Early: ~+13. OK, boost â +14 â 0.7 normalized.

Post-promo dip: day after promo values minus level: 95.97(-7), 97.33(-6), 102.68(0), 109.78(+8?), 90.52(-9), 93.66(-6), 92.15(-10), 96.71(-6), 102.01, 94.74, 96.42, 95.66(-8), 94.18(-9), 96.75, 95.41, 92.76(-12), 96.90, 96.86, 98.32, 100.38(-4), 99.18(-7), 99.93(-9), 103.16(-4), 102.71(-6), 100.36(-9), 99.14(-10), 98.69(-13), 97.67(-11), 104.12(-11), 106.83(-8), 106.20(-8), 106.20...

So post-promo dip â -8 (0.4 normalized). This matters both for (a) EMA contamination? Noâpromo day values are high, day-after values are low; on average they partly cancel? If promo day +14 and next day -8, sum over two days +6. In an EMA this biases level upward by (14-8)Â·freq... freq 13%: net bias â 0.13Â·(14Â·w...) roughly +0.8? Smallish.

More important: when predicting day t, if day t-1 was promo, expected y_t = level - 8 (dip) if t not promo. If t is promo and t-1 promo (consecutive promos happen), boost applies.

Can the LSTM capture this? Yes with design: track flag_{t} from previous row, then combine: prediction = EMA_level + p_tÂ·0.7 - p_{t-1}Â·0.4 + promo-interaction? Consecutive promo days: day 92 value 110.42 after 118.19 â second promo day lower. Day 261: 110.75 after 120.39. Day 478: 116.98 after 119.10. Day 520: 121.86 after 128.00. So second consecutive promo â first - 7. So if p_t=1 and p_{t-1}=1: boost â +14-7=+7? i.e., prediction = level + 0.7 - 0.35.

Also EMA contamination from promo-day values: our EMA includes promo days' inflated values and dips. Net small. But we can also correct: subtract 0.7Â·p_s from value before averaging (we know p_s one row late). That would make the EMA cleaner. Let's consider implementing: value path input v, plus memory of previous flag. We have flag in current row = p_{s+1}. We remember it; next step, effective value = v_{s+1} - 0.7Â·p_{s+1}(remembered). Then EMA tracks "baseline". Then output adds 0.7Â·p_t (from last row's flag) minus 0.4Â·p_{t-1} (remembered from last row... wait, last row's flag is p_t; the remembered flag at the last step is p_t? Let's trace.

Rows: row for s: [v_s, p_{s+1}]. Processing row s: we see v_s and p_{s+1}. We can store p_{s+1} in a memory unit updated at this step. At the next step (row s+1) we have remembered p_{s+1} and see v_{s+1}: effective value u_{s+1} = v_{s+1} - 0.7Â·p_{s+1} â but wait, we also want to correct v for the promo of its own day: v_s is promo-inflated iff p_s=1, and p_s was seen in row s-1. So at step s we remember p_{s+1} and could have remembered p_s from row s-1. So effective u_s = v_s - 0.7Â·p_s where p_s was stored at step s-1. So we need a one-step-delayed flag memory. Cell state naturally provides: cell1_t holds p_{t} (the flag seen in row t-1... hmm indices).

Let me define processing steps indexed by rows s = t-35 ... t-1. At step s, inputs v_s, p_{s+1}.

Memory unit 1: cell c1 updated to p_{s+1} each step: c1_new = p_{s+1} (input gate 1, forget 0, g = p_{s+1}-ish). Since pâ{0,1}, g = tanh(wÂ·p + b): choose wÂ·1+b = atanh... we want g=p. tanh(z)=p â z = atanh(p): for p=1, tanhâ1 needs large z; p=0 â z=0. Set g input weight for promo = 3, bias 0: tanh(3)=0.995â1, tanh(0)=0. Good. i=1 (bias big), f=0 (bias very negative). Then c1 = p_{s+1} after step s. So during step s+1, c1 (before update) holds p_{s+1} = p at day (s+1) = flag of the day whose value v_{s+1} we're now seeing. 

So value path at step s: effective value u_s = v_s - 0.7Â·(flag stored from previous step = p_s). We can implement in the cell gate of unit 0: g0 = tanh(AÂ·v_s + BÂ·p_s(?) ...) â but p_s isn't an input at step s; it's in c1 (memory from previous step). Cell input can use h_prev via W_hh. But h_prev = oÂ·tanh(c_prev), and c1_prev = p_s. If oâ1 and tanh(c1)âp_s (values 0/0.995), then h1_prev â p_s. 

So g0 = tanh(w_vÂ·v + w_hÂ·h1_prev + b). We want g0 â kÂ·(v - 0.7Â·p_s) for small values. Use linear approximation: tanh(z)âz for small z. Set w_v = k, w_h = -0.7k, b=0. With k=0.1 (to keep small). Then i0Â·g0 with i0 = Î²: c0_new = Î±Â·c0 + Î²Â·0.1Â·(v - 0.7 p_s). Choose Î± = 0.85, Î²Â·0.1 = 0.15 â Î² = 1.5 > 1 impossible (sigmoid â¤1). So reduce k? We need iÂ·g coefficient (1-Î±)=0.15 with k=0.1: i0 must be 1.5 â impossible. Instead set k = 0.3, i0 = 0.5: 0.5Â·0.3 = 0.15. But then g0 argument up to 0.3Â·(v-0.7p); v up to 2 â 0.6; tanh(0.6)=0.537 vs 0.6 â 10% error, and varies. Hmm.

Alternatively set Î± smaller: Î±=0.6, (1-Î±)=0.4, k=0.2, i0=... i0Â·k=0.4 â i0=2 impossible. i0 â¤1 always, so k â¥ 1-Î±. To keep tanh linear need kÂ·|v| small; v up to ~2, so kÂ·2 should be â¤0.3 â kâ¤0.15 â 1-Î± â¤ 0.15 â Î± â¥ 0.85. Then EMA window ~ 1/(1-Î±) â 7+ days. Î±=0.9, 1-Î±=0.1, k=0.15, i=0.667 â i bias = logit(0.667)=0.693. g0 = tanh(0.15Â·v - 0.105Â·p_s). Max arg 0.3 â tanh fine (error ~3% at extreme).

Actually we could also handle tanh nonlinearity by just accepting: g0 = tanh(0.15 v' ) where v' = v - 0.7p. tanh(0.15Â·v') vs 0.15Â·v': at v'=1: tanh(0.15)=0.1489 (0.7% low). Negligible! Great, 0.15 scaling keeps tanh quite linear. 

So c0 after processing: c0 â 0.15Â·EMA_{Î±=0.9}(v - 0.7 p). Range: v-0.7p mean ~0 to 0.6, std ~0.3 â c0 â ~[-0.1, 0.12]. tanh(c0)âc0. h0 = o0Â·tanh(c0), o0â1 â h0 â 0.15Â·baseline.

Now the promo adjustment at output: prediction z = baseline + 0.7Â·p_t - 0.35Â·p_{t-1}? Wait the dip: if p_{t-1}=1, y_t = level - 0.4 (normalized). And p_t=1: +0.7. If both: +0.7-0.35 â +0.35 (observed second-day promo â +7 = 0.35). Hmm but is the dip additive with promo? Second promo day â level + 7 â 0.35. And dip alone -0.4. If additive: level +0.7-0.4 = +0.3 â close to 0.35. Good, additive model: z = level + 0.7Â·p_t - 0.4Â·p_{t-1}.

At the final step (s = t-1): we see p_t as input. Need memory of p_t at output time. But h after final step: c1 updated with p_t (c1_new = p_t) â yes! Unit 1's cell is updated at each step to the current row's flag, so after the last step, c1 = p_t and h1 = p_t (with oâ1). 

And p_{t-1} is stored in... at final step, c1 before update = p_{t-1}, and h1_prev = p_{t-1} feeds into g0 computation at final step (correcting v_{t-1}) â. But for output we need p_{t-1} after the final step â it's overwritten in c1. So use a second memory unit: unit 2 with c2 updated to p_t but delayed by one: c2_new = h1_prev = p_{t-1}... Actually c2 at final step: update c2_new = (previous c1) = p_{t-1}. Implement: c2's cell gate g2 = tanh(wÂ·h1_prev) with w=3: g2 = p_{t-1} (0 or ~1). i2=1, f2=0. Then after final step c2 = p_{t-1}, h2 = p_{t-1}. 

Output: z = 10Â·h0 + 0.7Â·h1 - 0.4Â·h2 + b_out. Wait h0 â 0.15Â·baseline, so coefficient 1/0.15 = 6.667. Let me recompute: c0 = 0.15Â·EMA. Actually c0 = Î± c0 + iÂ·g where iÂ·(0.15 v') : i=0.667, gâ0.15 v' â contribution 0.1Â·v'. So c0 = 0.1Â·EMA(v'). Then W_out coefficient = 10. Let me redo: choose Î± (forget) = 0.9 via bias f: sigmoid(b_f)=0.9 â b_f = ln(9) = 2.197. i = 0.667 â b_i = 0.693. k=0.15 in g. Then steady state c0 = Î£ Î±^j Â· 0.667Â·0.15Â·v'_{...} = 0.1Â·EMA. Good. tanh(c0)âc0 (c0 â¤ ~0.13). h0 = oÂ·tanh(c0), o: sigmoid bias 2 â 0.881. Hmm o<1 reduces h0 by 12% â but constant factor, absorb into W_out: coefficient = 10/0.881 = 11.35. But o also depends on... make o constant: set output gate weights 0, bias 2.5 â o=0.924. Coefficient = 10/0.924 = 10.82. Let me just use bias 3 â o = 0.9526, coefficient = 10/0.9526 = 10.497 â 10.5. Also tanh(c0) â c0 - c0Â³/3: at c0=0.12, error 0.0006 relative to 0.12 â 0.5%. Fine.

Wait, also h0 feeds back into W_hh for other units â set those to 0 mostly. And c0's cell gate uses h1_prev (memory of p_s). Let me define units:

Unit 0: value EMA (baseline), with promo-corrected input.
Unit 1: current-row flag memory: c1 = p_{s+1} after step s.
Unit 2: previous flag: c2 = p_s during step s (i.e., stores flag from previous row).
Units 3-7: unused (zero weights, gates closed).

Actually wait: for g0 = tanh(kÂ·v - 0.7kÂ·p_s), we need p_s during step s = h1 at start of step s = o1Â·tanh(c1_prev) where c1_prev = p_s. Set o1 bias 3 â h1_prev â 0.95Â·tanh(p_s). tanh(3Â·1)... wait c1 stores p as tanh output? c1 = iÂ·g = tanh(3Â·p_input). For p=1: tanh(3)=0.9951. So c1 â {0, 0.9951}. tanh(c1) â c1 (tiny error). h1 = 0.9526Â·0.9951 = 0.948 when p=1. So effective stored value â0.948, not 1. Adjust coefficient: -0.7kÂ·0.948... The correction term: we want subtract 0.7Â·p_s in value units: contribution to c0: iÂ·tanh'(?)... g0 = tanh(kÂ·v + w_hh[0][1]Â·h1_prev). Want w_hh[0][1]Â·0.948 = -0.7Â·k = -0.105 â w_hh[0][1] = -0.1108. Hmm, but also when v is such that arg small, tanh linear. OK.

Similarly output uses h1 (p_t) and h2 (p_{t-1}): h1_final = 0.948Â·p_t approx (0.9526Â·0.9951). So W_out for unit1: 0.7/0.948 = 0.7385. Unit2: c2 = tanh(3Â·h1_prev): h1_prev = 0.948Â·p â tanh(2.845)=0.9929. h2 = 0.9526Â·0.9929 = 0.9459. W_out unit2: -0.4/0.946 = -0.4229.

Now details of gates:

Common: W_ih is [4H, 2] = [32,2], rows 0-7 input gate, 8-15 forget, 16-23 cell, 24-31 output. Columns: col0 = value v, col1 = promo flag p.

Unit 0 (value EMA):
- i0: sigmoid(b_i0) = 0.667 â b_i0 = ln(0.667/0.333) = ln(2) â 0.6931. Weights 0 (input-independent). Actually i should be constant: W_ih[0][*]=0, W_hh[0][*]=0, b_ih[0]=0.693, b_hh[0]=0.
- f0: sigmoid = 0.9 â b_f0 = ln(9) = 2.1972.
- g0 (cell): W_ih[16][0] = 0.15 (value), W_ih[16][1] = 0 (flag of next day â not needed for value correction; the value's own promo is p_s from memory). W_hh[16][1] = -0.1108 (h1_prev). b_ih[16] = 0, b_hh[16]=0.
- o0: sigmoid = 0.9526 â bias ln(0.9526/0.0474)= ln(20.1)=3.0. Set b=3.0.

Unit 1 (current flag memory):
- i1 = 1: bias large, 4.0 â sigmoid=0.982. Hmm want ~1. Use 5 â 0.9933. c1 = fÂ·c + iÂ·g = 0.9933Â·tanh(5p)... wait g1 = tanh(W_ih[17][1]Â·p + b). Want g1 = p: W_ih[17][1]... rows: cell rows are 16-23, unit1 cell row = 17. Set W_ih[17][1] = 5, b=0: p=1 â tanh(5)=0.9999; p=0 â 0. i1: b=5 â 0.9933. f1 = 0: b = -5 â 0.0067. c1 = 0.9933Â·0.9999Â·p â 0.993Â·p. Hmm, that reduces stored flag to 0.993 â fine, recompute coefficients: h1 = o1Â·tanh(c1): o1 b=3 â 0.9526. tanh(0.993)=0.758?? No wait â tanh(0.993) = 0.758!
